classes.name: Parish, town, and community council elections
classes.note: No source counts the parish, town, and community councils that voted each year, so this level lists no elections and holds only its gap rows. It sits ahead of the principal councils so a parish ward contest is never counted as one of them.

classes.name: Council elections
classes.note: Counted per council: each council that held its scheduled elections on the year's local polling day counts once, whether it elected every member or a third of them. By-elections don't count. England's figures come from the House of Commons Library, the Electoral Commission, and the Elections Centre's Local Elections Handbooks; Scotland's 32 councils, Wales's 22, and Northern Ireland's 26 (11 from 2014) are added in the years they voted. In 2012 Wales counts 21, because Anglesey's election was moved to 2013.

dates.note: England 37; Northern Ireland 26 (ni-2005: 'The elections for Northern Ireland's 26 local councils took place on 5 May, 2005'). dates.note: England 176. Academic research centre, not an official source. The same count appears in Rallings and Thrasher, Representation (2006).
dates.quote: In 2006 there were elections in England for a total of 176 local authorities comprising 32 London boroughs, 36 metropolitan boroughs, 20 unitary authorities and 88 shire districts.

dates.quote: In England, 312 local authorities held elections, the majority of which were of the whole council.

dates.note: England 137; Wales 22 (Senedd Research: 'A single tier of 22 unitary authorities was created'). Academic research centre, not an official source.
dates.quote: In 2008 there were elections in England for a total of 137 local authorities comprising 36 metropolitan boroughs, 19 current and 4 ‘shadow’ unitary authorities and 78 shire districts.

dates.note: England 128; Scotland 32 (Boundaries Scotland: 'The Local Government etc. (Scotland) Act 1994 created the 32 single-tier local government areas that cover Scotland.'); Wales 21 (22 unitary authorities less Anglesey, postponed to 2013 by SI 2012/686). Conflict: the Electoral Commission's Local elections and referendums in England 2012 report (July 2012, https://www.markpack.org.uk/files/2016/05/Electoral-Commission-Report-Into-May-2012-Elections.pdf, hosted copy) states 'On 3 May 2012 there were local elections to 103 local authorities in England.' The House of Commons Library briefing SN06194 (January 2012) gives 128 before the poll. The 128 figure is used here; the 103 figure is unexplained and should be checked against the report's data.

dates.note: England 143. The election was held on 6 May 2021, not in June as the brief stated. The Elections Centre Local Elections Handbook 2021 gives the same total (143 = 21 county + 28 unitary + 35 metropolitan + 59 district).

dates.note: England 146; Scotland 32 (Boundaries Scotland: 'The Local Government etc. (Scotland) Act 1994 created the 32 single-tier local government areas that cover Scotland.'); Wales 22 (Senedd Research: 'A single tier of 22 unitary authorities was created'). The Commons Library and the Elections Centre handbook (32 + 33 + 21 + 60 = 146) agree on 146, so 146 is used here.
dates.quote: England held elections in 146 councils, while all 32 councils in Scotland and 22 Welsh councils were up for election.

dates.quote: In 2024 there were elections for a total of 107 local authorities across England.

dates.note: England 23. The 2025 cycle was reduced because the government postponed nine county council elections to 2026.
